title: personal-aml-quant-eval-scratchpad
content:
2026-03-12 / quick scratchpad - quant + eval runs

Goal: quick notes while iterating on q8_0 vs q4f16 baseline for chat-like prompts. Focus: end-user quality (exact-match & helpfulness), latency/backpressure weirdness on dedicated nodes, and KV-cache interaction.

Experiments tried (chronological):
- run A: q8_0, batch=16, kv-cache=on, tokens/sample=120, runtime=redwood-hosted-default
  - CLI: python run_eval.py --model q8_0 --batch 16 --kv_cache true --input eval/prompts/chat-short.json --max_tokens 120 --seed 42
  - result: avg latency 210ms/token, 95p latency 450ms, fast but occasional spikes. automated eval: EM=0.71, BLEU-like=0.62, subjective-spot-check: 7/10 helpfulness.
  - notes: one sample had incoherent reference to prior context (possible KV mismatch).

- run B: q4f16, batch=8, kv-cache=on
  - CLI: python run_eval.py --model q4f16 --batch 8 --kv_cache true --input eval/prompts/chat-short.json --max_tokens 120
  - result: avg latency 310ms/token, 95p 680ms. EM=0.74 (slightly higher), hallucinations reduced in few-shot tests. CPU fallback observed on node-7 for 12s during one run (see logs).

- run C: q4f16, batch=8, kv-cache=off (explicitly disabled)
  - result: latency improved marginally for bursty requests (95p drops to 540ms). EM unchanged. Conclusion: kv-cache interacts badly with certain kernel selection paths in serving runtime for long context. TODO investigate kernel selection logs.

Prompt set notes:
- chat-short.json: 200 samples: user questions, follow-ups, style-system prompt included. Need to add more adversarial prompts (ambiguous references, long chain-of-thought).
- new prompt idea: include 'system-level clarifier' to force concision. Add 100 samples and re-run.

Open issues / immediate TODOs:
- [ ] ML-3721: reproduce CPU fallback locally on dedicated dev box; capture 'dmesg' + runtime trace. (linked ticket)
- [ ] Add regression test for KV-cache + quantized kernels (unit test harness in repro/bench). PR started in GH PR 459 but needs perf harness.
- [ ] Run batch sweep: batches = [1,2,4,8,16] x kv_cache=[on,off] for q4f16 and q8_0, log p95 and EM. Automation note: use flaky-runner to avoid noisy nodes.
- [ ] Add new prompt set 'chat-ambiguous-ref.json' with 120 samples. Assign to Diego.
- [ ] If CPU fallback persists, try kernel override env var: REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=avx2 (experiment in staging).

Quick commands I used (copy-paste):
- python run_eval.py --model q8_0 --batch 16 --kv_cache true --input eval/prompts/chat-short.json --max_tokens 120 --out results/q8_runA.json
- docker logs -f node-7 | grep -i kernel
- REDWOOD_KERNEL_DEBUG=1 REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=avx2 ./bin/serve_local --model-path /mnt/models/q4f16

Observations and hypotheses:
- Hypothesis 1: q4f16 reduces numeric error on LM head leading to fewer hallucinations; cost is slightly higher compute per token because of dequant path.
- Hypothesis 2: KV-cache path triggers an alternate kernel selection that isn't tested under our CI, causing rare CPU fallbacks on some nodes. Might be related to memory alignment with quantized tensors.
- Hypothesis 3: Batch size interacts with latency SLOs nonlinearly: bigger batches reduce average cost but increase p95 dramatically when queueing spikes occur.

Notes for write-up / next sync:
- Make a short doc for PS: include p95 vs EM plots for q8_0 vs q4f16, and list recommended default profiles per workload (chat-short vs code-completion).
- Prepare a small demo for eng-sre: reproduce CPU fallback on dedicated dev cluster, include kernel debug trace.

Misc small reminders:
- Add link to confluence page with eval definitions (TODO: update metrics section to include helpfulness subjective scoring rubric).
- Check-in with Alex about infra quota for longer eval runs (we may need additional GPU pool time next week).

Rough timeline:
- Mar 13: finish batch sweep automation + new prompt set creation.
- Mar 15: draft PS doc with plots + recommendations.
- Mar 20: present to infra + eng-sre if CPU fallback persists.

Scratchpad end.
